plan.notes: Source: official Merrimack College sample four-year schedule 'Computer Science, BS (Starting with Calculus)' curriculum map (https://www.merrimack.edu/wp-content/uploads/computer-science-bs-calculus-start-curriculum-map.pdf), linked from the official Merrimack CS major page as the 'Curriculum Guide' sample four-year schedule. The PDF is undated; degree minimums (124 credits to graduate, 64-credit major: 8 core + 8 elective-area courses, minimum 2.0 GPA) cross-verified against the current catalog's 'Program: Computer Science, B.S.' page (https://catalog.merrimack.edu/preview_program.php?catoid=20&poid=3065&returnto=536). Catalog year recorded as 2025-2026 (current catalog at time of collection); the map is the current official sequence. Transcription method: manual transcription of the published term-by-term map; course titles, credit values, and prerequisites verified against current catalog.merrimack.edu course descriptions. CREDIT TOTAL NOTE: the catalog publishes a 124-credit degree minimum, but the official map schedules 16 credits x 8 terms = 128 credits; total_credits uses the sequence's own published total (128) per precedent. Prerequisite grade details (from catalog course descriptions): CSC 2820 needs B- or better in CSC 1610 (alternatives: CSC 1611 or P in CSC 1010); CSC 2710 needs B- or better in CSC 2820 plus C or better in MTH 1314 (MTH 1217 corequisite satisfied in Year 1); CSC 2620 needs B- or better in CSC 2820; CSC 3810 needs B- or better in CSC 2820 or (P in CSC 1011 and MTH 1314); CSC 4910 needs CSC 2620 plus instructor permission and is offered every fall; MTH 1217 needs C- or better in MTH 1016 (Precalculus) or exemption via the Mathematics Placement Assessment; MTH 1314 needs a placement score of 28+ or MTH 1016. The map's 'FIC Core Course' label (Year 2 Fall) is a PDF typo for 'FC Core Course'. A separate official 'Starting with Algebra' map exists for students placing below calculus (https://www.merrimack.edu/wp-content/uploads/computer-science-bs-algebra-start-curriculum-map.pdf); this plan follows the standard calculus-start sequence. Experiential learning (internship/co-op/research/competition/study abroad registered with the O'Brien Center) is a catalog graduation requirement for CS majors; modeled as a 0-credit required milestone.
